title: Fetching Data
description: Learn patterns for fetching data from APIs in React.

data.text: Data fetching is one of the most common side effects in React. The pattern is consistent: trigger a fetch in useEffect, track loading and error state, and render the result when it arrives.
Every data-fetching component needs three pieces of state: the data itself, a loading flag, and an error message. Initialize them, fetch on mount, and render conditionally.

data.title: Basic Fetch
data.content: Loading data on mount with useEffect

data.text: Use AbortController to cancel the request when the component unmounts. This is cleaner than the isMounted flag and is the modern standard.

data.title: Abort Controller

data.text: When a dependency like a user ID changes, include it in the dependency array so React re-runs the effect and fetches fresh data.

data.title: Fetch on Dependency Change

data.text: Always handle three states: loading, error, and success. Users should never see a broken UI or a blank screen while data loads.

data.title: Use a Data Library in Production
data.text: For real apps, consider React Query (TanStack Query) or SWR. They handle caching, refetching, deduplication, and stale-while-revalidate automatically.

data.description: Fetch posts from a public API and display them with loading and error handling.
steps: Track loading, error, and success states.
Render a loading message, an error message, or a list of post titles.
data.expectedOutcome: A posts list that loads asynchronously with proper feedback for all states.

items.question: Why does my app crash with 'Can't perform a React state update on an unmounted component'?
items.answer: The fetch resolved after the component unmounted. Use AbortController or an isMounted flag to prevent setting state on unmounted components.

items.question: Should I put fetch in useEffect or use a library?
items.answer: For learning, useEffect teaches fundamentals. For production, React Query or SWR reduce boilerplate and add caching, retries, and background refetching.

items.question: How do I avoid race conditions?
items.answer: Use an AbortController or track the latest request ID in a ref. Ignore responses from earlier requests.

items.question: Can I fetch inside an event handler instead?
items.answer: Yes. Fetching in response to a user action (like clicking 'Load More') is also common and does not require useEffect.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Fetch data in useEffect with the proper dependency array.
Track loading, error, and data state.
Use AbortController to cancel requests on unmount.
Consider React Query or SWR for production data fetching.
data.takeaway: Data fetching is a core React skill. Next, you will extract this logic into reusable custom hooks.
